html:
A loose union of Turkic nomads that ruled the western Eurasian steppe from about the 11th century until the Mongol conquest. Its two main peoples were the Cumans, called Polovtsians by the Rus', and the Kipchaks. On the map in 1100 it stretches from the Black Sea to the Irtysh.

The Cumans pushed out the Pechenegs and then helped Byzantium destroy them at Levounion in 1091. With the princes of Kievan Rus' they raided, traded and intermarried in turn; a failed Rus' raid of 1185 is the subject of the Tale of Igor's Campaign. Georgian kings hired Kipchak soldiers in large numbers.

The Mongols beat a Rus' and Cuman army at the Kalka River in 1223 and conquered the steppe in the late 1230s. Many Cumans fled to Hungary. Those who stayed became the base population of the Golden Horde, whose language was Kipchak Turkic, and Kipchak slave soldiers later ruled Egypt as the Mamluks.
